correctness.rationale: The intrinsic zero-sum coordinate, dimension, metric inequalities and three projector normalizations are explicit. By uniqueness and central symmetry, the global John ellipsoid is centered; \(S_p\times S_q\) forces three invariant eigenspaces. Pairwise squared supports exactly equal \(2a\), \(2b\), and \(\alpha a+\beta b+\gamma c\). The volume maximizes \(a^{p-1}b^{q-1}c\) under three linear constraints. The three analytic branches have positive eigenvalues and satisfy exact primal feasibility, stationarity, nonnegative KKT multipliers and complementarity; strict log-det concavity proves global uniqueness. Cross and within-part contacts follow by equality, and an explicit potential witnesses strict ball enlargement during the ellipsoid plateau. The included standard-library checker reconstructs rational projector matrices for 2580 parameter cases, but it does not replace the general argument.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of objects and implications identifies the new assertion as the exact continuously parametrized John ellipsoid and its contact/saturation transitions, not the known endpoint or a facet count. The same-metric public full text supplies facet counts only; a complete-bipartite Hilbert-distance result supplies t=2 only. General D-optimal theory does not determine the constrained optimizer. Prior accessible own claims concern volumes, fixed split graphs, covariance, inballs, or endpoint ellipsoids and do not imply both new thresholds. No stronger equivalent coverage was identified in the completed searches; residual bibliographic uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier D-optimal-design, weighted graph polytope, or transportation norm paper could contain an equivalent formula under different terminology.
Publicly published material available without a bibliographic priority assessment is not proof of absolute mathematical novelty.

value.rationale: The John ellipsoid and its intrinsic Euclidean volume are fundamental, natural Banach-dual shape invariants for this metric family. The sharp two-stage loss of within-part support contacts for p<q, coalescence for p=q and pre-endpoint saturation despite strictly growing bodies explain a nontrivial inverse-geometric screening phenomenon. They are not a mere change of notation or a known special case of a general ellipsoid principle; the endpoint and classical background are separated from the new interior theorem.
